summary: `wake`'s `if (seq > w.sinceSeq)` can never be false, yet the class doc states it as a guarantee ("`wake` idempotently unparks it, and only a `seq` above `sinceSeq` may"). A reader has to reconstruct three separate facts from three other modules to learn the predicate is decorative, which is precisely the state CLAUDE.md's comment rule says to fix in the code rather than the comment.
failure: Traced, then confirmed by mutation. `wake` is called from exactly one place — `TelegramPlugin.ingest`, `this.waiters.wake(chatId, rec.seq)` — and only for a record `store.append` just stamped, so `rec.seq === store.highWater()` at that instant. A waiter's `sinceSeq` came from `requireOwnCursor`, which refuses anything above `store.highWater()` at park time, and `nextSeq` only increases. Therefore `seq > w.sinceSeq` holds for every reachable call. Mutation `for (const w of [...set]) w.wake();` (predicate deleted entirely): Test Files 28 passed, Tests 937 passed | 3 skipped — no input in the suite distinguishes the two, and none can exist.
remediation: Either delete the predicate and the clause of the doc that asserts it — `wake(chatId)` then honestly says "unpark every waiter on this chat, because ingest only ever calls it for a sequence above every cursor already issued" — or, if the guard is wanted as a genuine defence, move it where it can fail by parking on the CHAT'S tail (`store.maxSeq(chatId)`) rather than on a store-wide `since`, which makes a cross-chat cursor a reachable false case.
testUpgrade: The class is "a conditional whose false branch no input can reach, presented as a guarantee". Rather than a case, add this to the mutation set the package already implicitly relies on: a lint over `src/**` is the wrong shape here, but a standing rule for this suite is that every `if` in `waiters.ts`/`cursor.ts`/`store.ts` guarding a documented invariant must have a named case; the durable form is the parameterized refusal-invariance table proposed for store.ts:278, extended with a row per guard, so a guard with no row is visible as an omission rather than as green coverage.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: `cursor.ts` `if (seq > store.highWater()) { throw ... }` — this is the branch that makes the predicate unreachable-false, and deleting it (mutation `cursor-no-highwater`) IS caught by the suite, so the two are not independently removable.
remediationCheck.newlyAccepts: Deleting the predicate accepts nothing new: the set of waiters woken is identical for every reachable input.
remediationCheck.newlyRejects: none.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: none — verified by running the exact mutation that deletes the predicate; all 937 tests stayed green.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Cosmetic-to-comprehension only. If applied and I am wrong about unreachability, the consequence is a spuriously-woken `fetchRecent` that immediately re-queries and returns an empty page — which the seam explicitly permits ("returns early/empty is still correct"). That is why I traced the three facts rather than relying on the mutation alone.
remediationCheck.interleavings: The one ordering that could make the predicate matter is a `wake` racing a `park` for the same chat. JS is single-threaded and both `ingest` and the `park` registration run synchronously with no await between the emptiness check and the executor, so two callers cannot interleave inside either. A second caller parking on the same chat while a first is being woken sees the snapshot `[...set]`, so it is not woken by the in-flight call and waits for the next ingest.

summary: `fetchRecent` passes `args.blockMs` straight to `Waiters.park` -> `setTimeout` with no finiteness or range screen, where bridge-discord (`const blockMs = Number.isFinite(asked) ? asked : 0;`) and bridge-matrix both screen it, each citing "the seam declares `blockMs?: number` with no bound". The seam type is `number`, not a clamped one, so strictness at the plugin boundary is the house rule here.
failure: `fetchRecent({ topic, since, blockMs: Infinity })` (or any value above 2^31-1) reaches `setTimeout(wake, Infinity)`. Verified against Node: it prints `TimeoutOverflowWarning: Infinity does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer. Timeout duration was set to 1.` on stderr and fires after 1ms. stderr is the operator's diagnostic channel (stdout is JSON-RPC), so the observable result is an un-prefixed Node warning in the bridge's log and a long-poll that silently does not block. Not reachable through core's MCP path today — `catchup.block_max_ms` is clamped to MAX_BLOCK_MS in bridge-core/src/config.ts — so this is reachable by a direct embedder and by the conformance harness, not by a model.
remediation: Mirror the sibling plugins at the top of `query`: `const asked = args.blockMs ?? 0; const blockMs = Number.isFinite(asked) ? Math.max(0, Math.floor(asked)) : 0;` and use `blockMs` in both the `> 0` test and the `park` call. Do NOT invent a plugin-side ceiling — core owns the clamp; the screen is only for values the arithmetic is not defined on.
testUpgrade: The class is "a numeric seam argument used without normalization". `cursor.ts`'s `requireLimit` already owns this discipline for `limit` and is graded by hostile-text.test.ts's limit channel; widen that channel into a table over every numeric seam field — `limit` and `blockMs` today — crossed with a generator of out-of-domain values (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `-1`, `-0`, `1e21`, `2**31`, `1.5`) and assert the call either rejects with a named message or returns within a bound, and that no un-prefixed line reaches stderr. A third numeric field added to the seam then inherits the whole generator.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: The existing `args.blockMs !== undefined && args.blockMs > 0` test, which already excludes `NaN` (`NaN > 0` is false) — so the fix's only new effect is on `Infinity` and on values above the 32-bit range.
remediationCheck.newlyAccepts: `blockMs: 1.5` would be floored to 1 rather than passed fractional; `blockMs: Infinity` becomes a non-blocking call with no Node warning, where today it is a 1ms block WITH a warning. Both are behaviourally closer to what the caller could predict.
remediationCheck.newlyRejects: none — the fix normalizes, it does not reject. A stricter variant that threw on non-finite `blockMs` would newly reject `blockMs: Infinity`, which today resolves; I did not choose that because the seam calls `blockMs` a HINT and throwing on a hint is its own astonishment.
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: none found. I grepped the package's tests for `blockMs` usage: the conformance blocking case passes 2000/5000/SINCELESS_BLOCK_MS/IDLE_BLOCK_MS, and push-delivery/fetch-args pass finite integers. None is affected by flooring or by the non-finite arm.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: Applied, the Node warning and the surprising 1ms 'block' both go away. Nothing stays broken, because nothing depends on the current behaviour. The one thing it does NOT fix is the underlying asymmetry — three plugins screen this and one does not — which is a seam-shape observation: if every plugin must screen the same field the same way, the normalization belongs beside `requireLimit` or in core, not copy-pasted a fourth time.
